summary: Naproxen is a long-acting NSAID used for inflammatory arthritis, acute pain, dysmenorrhea and acute gout. Typical dosing is 250-500 mg twice daily with food. It carries a boxed warning for serious cardiovascular thrombotic events and GI bleeding; use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.
indications: Rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis

dosage.d: 250-500 mg (naproxen) twice daily; may increase to 1500 mg/day for up to 6 months
550 mg naproxen sodium then 550 mg q12h or 275 mg q6-8h
dosage.n: First-day total up to 1375 mg sodium salt

dosage.d: 750 mg naproxen then 250 mg q8h until attack subsides
dosage.n: Or 825 mg sodium then 275 mg q8h

admin: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Take with food, milk or an antacid to minimize gastrointestinal upset
Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water; do not lie down for 10 minutes after
Naproxen 200 mg = naproxen sodium 220 mg (account for salt form when dosing)
Do not combine with other NSAIDs or aspirin for analgesia
moa: Naproxen non-selectively inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 and cyclooxygenase-2, reducing the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins. Decreased prostaglandin synthesis produces anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antipyretic effects but also accounts for gastrointestinal and renal adverse effects.

absolute: History of asthma, urticaria or allergic reaction after aspirin/NSAIDs
Setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
relative: Active peptic ulcer or GI bleeding

preg: Avoid NSAIDs from about 20 weeks gestation (risk of fetal renal dysfunction/oligohydramnios) and contraindicated from 30 weeks due to premature closure of the ductus arteriosus. Use during the first half of pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Naproxen is excreted in human milk. Because of potential adverse effects in nursing infants, avoid where possible or choose an alternative; weigh benefit against risk.
renal: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins and can precipitate acute kidney injury, especially in volume depletion, heart failure or pre-existing renal disease. Not recommended in advanced renal disease (CrCl <30 mL/min); monitor renal function in at-risk patients.
hepatic: Use with caution; rare severe hepatic reactions (jaundice, hepatitis) can occur. Reduce dose and monitor in hepatic impairment; discontinue if liver disease develops or transaminases rise persistently.

major: Other NSAIDs/aspirin - increased GI and bleeding risk
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect, renal impairment (triple whammy)
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce gastric irritation; food may slightly delay absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
interactions.diagnostics: May interfere with 17-ketogenic steroid assays and urinary 5-HIAA tests; stop temporarily before such testing.

monitoring: Blood pressure at baseline and periodically
Renal function (serum creatinine) in at-risk patients
Hemoglobin/hematocrit if signs of GI bleeding or with long-term use
Liver enzymes if symptoms of hepatotoxicity
counsel: Take with food, milk or antacid to protect the stomach
Stop and seek care for black/tarry stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, weakness or slurred speech
Avoid alcohol and other NSAIDs/aspirin while taking naproxen
Report swelling, unexplained weight gain or shortness of breath
Use the lowest dose for the shortest time needed
pearls: BOXED WARNING: serious CV thrombotic events (MI, stroke) and GI bleeding/perforation; contraindicated peri-CABG
Longer half-life than ibuprofen allows convenient twice-daily dosing
Among NSAIDs, naproxen may carry comparatively lower CV thrombotic risk but is not risk-free
Naproxen base 200 mg = naproxen sodium 220 mg; check the salt form when prescribing
Avoid the triple-whammy combination of NSAID + ACEi/ARB + diuretic
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Symptoms include drowsiness, heartburn, nausea, vomiting and epigastric pain; rarely seizures or renal failure. There is no specific antidote. Treat supportively, consider activated charcoal within 1 hour of a large ingestion, and protect the airway. Hemodialysis is not effective due to high protein binding.
